knowledge:
- key_parameters: is.counts=Set to TRUE in M3DropConvertData or NBumiConvertData if the input matrix contains raw counts ;; is.log=Set to TRUE in M3DropConvertData if the input matrix is log-transformed ;; pseudocount=The pseudocount used during log-transformation (e.g., 1) to correctly de-log the data ;; mt_method=Multiple testing correction method (e.g., "fdr") in M3DropFeatureSelection ;; mt_threshold=Significance threshold (e.g., 0.01) for identifying differentially expressed genes in M3DropFeatureSelection ;; method=Multiple testing correction method in NBumiFeatureSelectionCombinedDrop ;; qval.thres=Significance threshold for the DANB model feature selection ;; k=Number of clusters to extract from the heatmap dendrogram in M3DropGetHeatmapClusters ;; type=Type of clustering to extract ("cell" or "gene") in M3DropGetHeatmapClusters
- alternatives: BrenneckeGetVariableGenes=Identifies highly variable genes based on the relationship between CV2 and mean expression, but is more sensitive to lowly expressed genes and can overestimate variability of highly expressed genes ;; giniFS=Feature selection based on GiniClust ;; pcaFS=Feature selection based on monocle using irlba and sparse matrices ;; corFS=Feature selection using gene-gene correlations ;; Consensus_FS=Combines all available feature selection methods by taking the average rank of genes across methods
- when_to_use: Use the Michaelis-Menten model (M3Drop) for full-transcript single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-seq2) without UMIs that has been sequenced to near saturation (>100,000 reads per cell). Use the depth-adjusted negative binomial model (NBumi) for UMI-tagged single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Chromium) where dropouts are often driven by low sequencing coverage.
- pitfalls: Do not use the Michaelis-Menten model (M3Drop) on UMI-tagged data, as it struggles to fit data not sequenced to saturation. Do not use the DANB model (NBumi) on full-transcript data with high amplification noise, as its simplified noise model will be too permissive and identify too many false positives. M3Drop requires a normalized but not log-transformed expression matrix, whereas NBumi requires raw counts.

workflows.name: non_umi_m3drop_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform dropout-based feature selection, cell clustering, and marker gene identification for non-UMI single-cell RNA-seq data using the Michaelis-Menten model.
input: counts (raw count matrix or normalized expression matrix from non-UMI scRNA-seq data)
labels (character vector of cell labels or timepoints)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter low-quality cells based on minimum detected genes ;; 2. Convert and normalize raw counts to a non-log-transformed expression matrix using M3DropConvertData ;; 3. Perform feature selection using M3DropFeatureSelection ;; 4. Visualize selected features using M3DropExpressionHeatmap ;; 5. Cluster cells from the heatmap using M3DropGetHeatmapClusters ;; 6. Identify marker genes for the clusters using M3DropGetMarkers
workflows.code:
counts <- Mmus_example_list$data
labels <- Mmus_example_list$labels
total_features <- colSums(counts >= 0)
counts <- counts[,total_features >= 2000]
labels <- labels[total_features >= 2000]
norm <- M3DropConvertData(counts, is.counts=TRUE)
norm <- M3DropConvertData(log2(norm+1), is.log=TRUE, pseudocount=1)
M3Drop_genes <- M3DropFeatureSelection(norm, mt_method="fdr", mt_threshold=0.01)
heat_out <- M3DropExpressionHeatmap(M3Drop_genes$Gene, norm, cell_labels = labels)
cell_populations <- M3DropGetHeatmapClusters(heat_out, k=4, type="cell")
library("ROCR") 
marker_genes <- M3DropGetMarkers(norm, cell_populations)
head(marker_genes[marker_genes$Group==4,],20) 
marker_genes[rownames(marker_genes)=="Cdx2",]

workflows.name: umi_nbumi_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform dropout-based feature selection and calculate Pearson residuals for UMI-tagged single-cell RNA-seq data using the depth-adjusted negative binomial (DANB) model.
workflows.stages: 1. Convert and format raw counts using NBumiConvertData ;; 2. Fit the depth-adjusted negative binomial model using NBumiFitModel ;; 3. Check model fit using NBumiCheckFitFS ;; 4. Perform feature selection using NBumiFeatureSelectionCombinedDrop ;; 5. Calculate exact or approximate Pearson residuals using NBumiPearsonResiduals or NBumiPearsonResidualsApprox ;; 6. Clip residuals to reduce the effect of extreme outliers
workflows.code:
count_mat <- NBumiConvertData(Mmus_example_list$data, is.counts=TRUE)
DANB_fit <- NBumiFitModel(count_mat)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
stats <- NBumiCheckFitFS(count_mat, DANB_fit)
print(c(stats$gene_error,stats$cell_error))
NBDropFS <- NBumiFeatureSelectionCombinedDrop(DANB_fit, method="fdr", qval.thres=0.01, suppress.plot=FALSE)
pearson1 <- NBumiPearsonResiduals(count_mat, DANB_fit)
pearson2 <- NBumiPearsonResidualsApprox(count_mat, DANB_fit)
pearson1[pearson1 > sqrt(ncol(count_mat))] <- sqrt(ncol(count_mat))
pearson1[pearson1 < -sqrt(ncol(count_mat))] <- -1*sqrt(ncol(count_mat))
